title: Operational Collapse Region in Repeaterless Loss-Dephasing Quantum Channels
authors: Ufuk Korkmaz, S. Elham Mousavigharalari, Deniz Türkpençe
abstract: The distribution of entangled photon pairs over standard optical fiber is a fundamental requirement for the realization of the quantum internet. However, real-world deployment is severely bottlenecked by the interplay of amplitude damping (photon loss) and phase noise (birefringence). In this paper, we numerically investigate the degradation of dual-rail polarization entanglement in telecom C-band fiber links. We demonstrate a critical disparity between the physical survival of quantum correlations and their practical utility in standard communication protocols. By evaluating the unconditional logarithmic negativity against the post-selected teleportation fidelity, we identify a distinct ``operational collapse region'' -- a distance window where the channel retains true quantum entanglement, yet standard coincidence-based detection architectures fail to provide any advantage over classical strategies. Furthermore, we reveal that the width of this inaccessible region exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the phase noise rate, implying that simply minimizing fiber dephasing does not necessarily optimize the operational efficiency of the network. These findings provide vital guidelines for the design of practical quantum communication links.
summary: This paper analyzes the degradation of entanglement in optical fiber links by comparing two metrics: physical entanglement ($\mathcal{E}_N$) and practical utility ($F_{tele}$). It identifies an 'operational collapse region' where quantum correlations exist but cannot be exploited by standard detectors. The findings reveal that this operational gap width depends non-monotonically on the environmental phase noise, guiding future designs for robust quantum communication links.
main_problem: The study investigates the critical gap between the physical survival of quantum entanglement and its actual usability in standard communication protocols over lossy optical fibers.
main_result: A distinct 'operational collapse region' exists where true entanglement persists but coincidence-based detection fails to provide a quantum advantage, and this gap width depends non-monotonically on phase noise.
method: The authors numerically analyze the evolution of entangled states using Lindblad master equations, comparing two metrics: unconditional logarithmic negativity ($\mathcal{E}_N$) and post-selected teleportation fidelity ($F_{tele}$).
model_or_system: The system models dual-rail polarization entanglement transmitted through standard telecom C-band optical fibers, incorporating amplitude damping (photon loss) and pure dephasing noise.
key_observables: Unconditional logarithmic negativity ($\mathcal{E}_N$), post-selected teleportation fidelity ($F_{tele}$), and the width of the operational collapse region ($\Delta d$).
important_parameters: Photon loss rate ($\alpha$), phase noise rate ($\gamma_\phi$), and critical thresholds for entanglement/fidelity.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes standard coincidence-based detection architectures, which limits the measurable quantum advantage.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows distance-resolved dynamics comparing $\mathcal{E}_N$ (blue) and $F_{tele}$ (red), highlighting the shaded 'operational collapse region' ($R_{dead}$). Figure 2 illustrates how the width of this gap ($\Delta d$) changes non-monotonically with the phase noise rate ($\gamma_\phi$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using a Lindblad equation, defines two distinct metrics for entanglement survival and operational utility, calculates the resulting 'operational collapse region' ($R_{dead}$), and finally analyzes how varying the dephasing rate causes this gap width to change non-monotonically.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete guidelines on channel limitations in quantum networking, showing that optimizing one noise source (like minimizing dephasing) is insufficient if it exacerbates another operational bottleneck related to detection schemes.

figures.caption: Fig. 2. Post-selection success probability psucc(d) (black curve) for a symmetric telecom channel with α = 0.2 dB/km (κ ≈0.046 km−1). Colored bands indicate Rdead for four values of the dephasing rate: γφ ∈{0.20, 0.08, 0.06, 0.04} km−1. Each band spans [dF , dE], where dF is deﬁned by Ftele(dF ) = 2/3 + δF (δF = 10−3) and dE by EN (dE) = εEN (εEN = 10−4). The gap width ∆d reaches a maximum of 5.1 km at γφ = 0.08 km−1 and contracts at both higher and lower dephasing rates.
